feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It is clear and well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools add credibility.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are aligned and relevant to target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than measurable business impact (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption, cost savings).  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation varies between lists (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler. No major misspellings found, but formatting in the footer/project section is cramped and harder to scan.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper differentiation and one or two concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening to avoid repeating the subtitle; focus on distinctive value, not a generic leadership summary.
- Add 1–2 concrete scale markers from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Replace “Leads” with “Led” or “Has led” for tense consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Possible rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Has led enterprise website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and multimedia systems for mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “governance models,” and the capability list repeat content already covered in the subtitle and core competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with both Recent Projects and skills; keep it only if you want AI to be a headline theme.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward senior leadership scope rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g. use noun-led categories throughout.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and workflow integration.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows, replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with recent AI search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it broader and avoid tool-level detail already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is close to repeated messaging in both the header and experience sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinguishing details will make the footer feel additive rather than redundant.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Prioritize the most recent freelance work first and use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Replace vague phrases like “improve discovery” and “designed for continued campaign growth” with clearer outcomes if available (for example, faster access, reusable campaign framework, expanded engagement).
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot,” include serial commas consistently, and keep capitalization/title formatting uniform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; consider reframing them as named examples rather than restating responsibilities.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; it helps diversify the footer.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project section. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-led statements, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by streamlining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-team publishing processes.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats language already covered in the summary and NACo roles.
- Specific projects like AI search and microsites may duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry focused on role-level impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary focused on scope and leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight into one impact-oriented bullet and add outcomes if available: email open/click rates, social growth/engagement, video output, or cost savings from in-house production.
- Rewrite for stronger action/results phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten governance/analytics bullets by linking tools to business value: faster reporting, better campaign decisions, reduced publishing errors, improved cross-team planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video program growth overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on building the studio and scaling capacity.
- General digital channel management repeats earlier NACo roles; emphasize enterprise modernization, analytics infrastructure, and governance here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, channel ownership, and systems-building at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with systems language: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve…” is too soft and overlaps with governance/workflow language in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme fit, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. Tighten it to emphasize distinctive leadership scope rather than repeating broad digital/communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing systems
- Cross-channel content operations and campaign leadership
- Audience-centered messaging for advocacy and member communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and editorial planning” if you want stronger alignment with your recent leadership roles.
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid broad terms like “communications leadership” unless paired with scope or function.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize highest-value, recent platform strengths and execution capabilities rather than repeating every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool dump to a sharper value-led list: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

- Consider grouping by capability, not platform count: “Enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • Technical implementation • Integrations and automation • AI search”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

Suggested edit:

- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards & decision support.”

Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo role bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environment and production scope rather than basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery**

- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies; use “webcast production” or “live event delivery” to reduce repetition

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it more concise and current, with emphasis on strongest/recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space is tight, shorten further to: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages** and drop GitHub Pages unless it was used meaningfully in recent roles.
- Put **Drupal first** and consider bolding it, since it is clearly the most recent and highest-impact platform across current consulting and NACo leadership roles.
- If this section allows light qualifiers, add only one high-value descriptor tied to recency/scale, not multiple parentheticals.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the same platform list already under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- To avoid repetition, keep platforms here and use the Topline Skills version for broader capabilities (e.g., CMS modernization, APIs, automation).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the more current tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for delivery/operations: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, replace older/general terms with stronger specificity tied to recent work, e.g. “custom Drupal theming,” “serverless scripts,” “deployment automation,” or “tracking implementation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use that level of specificity; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if you want this section focused purely on build/implementation

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp”
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 lower-value names with outcome-oriented context elsewhere in experience bullets (e.g., built cross-team planning systems, automated reporting/workflows)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support a broader systems/operations story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter and campaign automation
- Keep the most relevant/current platform first; if Dynamics was the primary recent system, leave as ordered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign management” here if those points are already covered in Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat analytics/automation language that is already captured under Data, Analytics & Optimization or Automation & Workflow Systems.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize technical tools here and move broader capabilities into the skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • Google Optimize/experiment tools
- Replace broad nouns like “Dashboarding” with specific platforms or methods; if no dedicated tool, use “KPI reporting” or “performance reporting.”
- Consider changing “SEO” to “technical SEO” or “search performance analysis” for more specificity.
- Only keep “A/B testing” if you’ve directly run experiments; otherwise use “conversion analysis” or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- “Dashboarding” and “SEO” are already implied by your recent NACo analytics bullet, so keep this section tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it clearly foundational: team-building, early platform/content execution, and any concrete scale or output.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, growth in output, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; specify what changed (e.g., publishing process, content calendar, production cadence).
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing and production workflows while guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on establishing the program, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating governance/editorial workflow language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and underplays outcomes. Since later NACo roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support and the podcast as a distinct first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more specific, e.g. “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or result: number of episodes, audiences served, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded communications capacity.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then podcast/media execution second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles (video, digital content, production leadership).
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; later roles show the progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the most credible production capabilities framed more specifically.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing/production
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production” or, if accurate, “Studio and livestream production” for cleaner phrasing.
- Keep this item tool/capability-focused; avoid broader wording that belongs in experience bullets.
